transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — Maya from Redwood Inference. little note, we have Priya and Jon on for the technical pieces. uh, can we quickly go around?
[00:08] Evan: Evan Ross here, head of search at Zephyr Data. we've been evaluating vector relevance for our product search.
[00:12] Lina: Lina, ML engineer, working on rerank pipelines.
[00:15] Samir: Samir, CTO, I might drop in and out.
[00:20] Maya: Great. quick agenda — show hosted API embeddings, then rerank endpoint flow, Console metrics, and Optimize suggestions for cost/latency. questions anytime.
[00:36] Priya: I'll start with embeddings — our embeddings endpoint returns 1024-d vectors by default for the models we host but you can choose 512 or 2048 variants depending on model family. example call: POST /v1/embeddings with doc text, we return base64 vec or json floats, depends on your preferences.
[01:02] Lina: Quick question — dimension size is fixed per model, right? can we down-project?
[01:08] Priya: correct, fixed per chosen model. you can post-process with PCA on your side, or use our built-in projection recipe in Optimize to down-project for smaller indexes.
[01:25] Jon: For indexing we typically recommend HNSW for live QPS; we also provide batch import helpers if you're ingesting millions. We surfaced a connector pattern for S3 -> Redwood ingestion in the docs.
[01:43] Evan: ok, and about rerank — are you doing a two-stage: retrieve then rerank? or a single RPC?
[01:49] Priya: best practice is two-stage. call embeddings for retrieval (ANN), then send top-K candidates to our reranker endpoint which scores on context+query. reranker takes the original doc text and query, returns scores and you can pull final ordering. we offer both synchronous and streaming responses.
[02:11] Evan: latency numbers?
[02:13] Priya: typical rerank on our hosted endpoint is 40–110ms per document depending on model size and sequence lengths. for batch rerank (top 50) you can expect 200–700ms. these are median-ish in our benchmarks.
[02:29] Lina: that's a wide range; what's the tail?
[02:31] Priya: p95 ranges ~500–1.2s for big models but you can pin to smaller model variant for more predictable latency. also batching and prefix/KV cache help a lot for repeated contexts.
[02:46] Samir: what about cost — tokens and vector ops? our cost sensitivity is pretty high.
[02:51] Jon: hosted pricing is per-embedding unit and per-rerank call plus data transfer. we'll send a sample cost sheet. Optimize will give suggestions — like switching to 512-d embeddings for queries and QUANTIZED 8-bit variants for ranker to cut compute.
[03:09] Evan: do you support on-the-fly quantization or do models need to be compiled ahead?
[03:14] Priya: runtime supports several quantization profiles. some profiles are JIT applied, others we recommend doing at deployment/compile time for max throughput. we'll share recommended profiles per model.
[03:27] Lina: security — does hosted API keep data? we need no retention and SOC 2 compliance.
[03:33] Maya: we have SOC 2 Type II, customer data retention policies can be configured — by default short-term KV/prefix cache lives but you can opt-out of storage. for enterprise we have VPC/private deployment and bring-your-own-KMS options.
[03:50] Samir: SSO and RBAC?
[03:53] Maya: SSO via SAML/SCIM available for Enterprise plus role-based access in Console. audit logs are exportable to your SIEM.
[04:04] Evan: good. can the rerank call attach tooling like explainability or feature attributions?
[04:10] Priya: we can return scores and attention-like saliency in experimental models; but it's heavier so it increases latency. we also provide structured outputs to map fields for your UI.
[04:26] Lina: on the retrieval side, how do we evaluate recall vs rerank overhead?
[04:30] Jon: typical pattern: aim for recall@k ~ 0.95 with k=50 then rerank to push precision up. We ran mrr and ndcg tests; we'll help with a bench harness in the pilot.
[04:46] Evan: do you support approximate search backends? like Faiss vs your managed ANN?
[04:50] Priya: under the hood our embeddings pipeline is compatible with multiple indexers (Faiss, HNSW, Annoy). Hosted offers managed ANN with autoscaling; you can also bring an index from your infra and call our reranker only.
[05:04] Samir: what's the simplest integration for us to try?
[05:07] Maya: two options — quick start hosted: couple of API calls and sample code in Node/Python to do retrieve+rerank. second is a pilot where you give sample data, we run a bench and share a dashboard.
[05:22] Evan: we prefer the pilot with our sample corpus. ideally run both accuracy and latency metrics.
[05:27] Priya: makes sense — for the pilot we'll need 10k curious queries + corpus. also tell us target p95 latency SLO and cost ceiling.
[05:38] Evan: target p95 ~ 600ms for end-to-end rerank, and monthly cost under $X (redacted).
[05:45] Priya: noted. we'll propose a config: 512-d query embeddings, HNSW index, top-50 retrieval then a quantized reranker model.
[05:58] Lina: how does Console show cost breakdown?
[06:02] Jon: Console has per-route token cost, per-model runtime breakdown, and cohort-level usage — you can filter by API key or route. Optimize flags high-cost routes and suggests batching or quantization.
[06:17] Evan: any gotchas around batch vs online? we do some live suggestions so latency matters.
[06:22] Priya: for low-latency, avoid large batching. our SmartBatcher respects per-route latency SLOs to batch opportunistically. Optimize recommends batch sizes per traffic pattern.
[06:36] Samir: curious about fallback strategies if a model is constrained.
[06:40] Priya: Smart routing can fallback to a cheaper model variant or a cached response. we also support region failover for availability.
[06:50] Evan: competitors — how do you compare to Pinecone?
[06:53] Maya: Pinecone is index-first; Redwood is end-to-end inference plus rerank and observability — so fewer moving pieces for rerank-heavy flows. we also provide cost control levers and rollouts.
[07:06] Lina: re: embeddings drift — can you help retrain / refresh?
[07:11] Jon: we recommend periodic re-embedding with incremental indexing; Optimize can alert on embedding quality regressions tied to eval prompts.
[07:23] Evan: ok. can you show a quick demo of the rerank API call flow?
[07:28] Priya: sure — sharing screen. (screen share noises) here's a demo script: call embeddings endpoint, take results IDs, call /v1/rerank with payload {query, candidates: [{id, text}, ...]}. response is [{id, score, explanation?}].
[07:50] Priya: note sometimes transcription says kay vee cache — that's 'KV cache' in docs — we use ephemeral KV caches to speed repeated contexts.
[07:58] Lina: example payload size?
[08:01] Priya: typical topK 50 with each doc ~1.5k tokens — payload ~75k tokens. you'll want chunking for very long docs.
[08:12] Evan: what's the token accounting on rerank? query+candidate tokens count toward compute billing?
[08:16] Jon: yeah rerank counts tokens processed by the model. Console shows token-level cost. Optimize can recommend chunking/caching to reduce repeat costs.
[08:31] Samir: any examples of customers with similar scale?
[08:34] Maya: yes, a mid-market ecommerce firm did 2-stage retrieval+rerank and reduced average end-to-end latency 30% while improving hit precision. we can share anonymized metrics.
[08:47] Lina: how customizable are rerank scoring functions? can we inject our features?
[08:51] Priya: you can attach metadata and scalar features per candidate; reranker can condition on those fields. there is a callback pattern to include your business signals.
[09:05] Evan: storage — do you keep vectors?
[09:08] Maya: in hosted we persist vectors unless you opt out; for strict controls we recommend Dedicated or Private which give more isolation and retention control.
[09:20] Priya: also worth noting: for multi-tenant hosted we have SLA tiers; Dedicated gives guaranteed capacity and lower p95.
[09:30] Evan: okay. next steps?
[09:33] Maya: we'll send pricing + sample requests, Priya will drop config and bench harness, Evan will upload sample data. we'll target a kickoff next week.
[09:41] Samir: sounds good — appreciate the quick walk.
[09:44] Maya: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the pilot doc and timeline.
[09:48] (call ends)
